message.content: The total number of distinct positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of 10⁴³ legal positions (often referred to as the “Shannon number”). In other words, there are roughly ten‑to‑the‑forty‑third different ways the pieces can be arranged on the board during a legal game.
